post.description: Step 1: email + password. Answers the second steps on offer (TOTP first; email code fallback).
Step 2 with the authenticator app: `mfa=true` (needed for approvals, price edits, settings).
Fallback second step: a 6-digit code to the staff member's work address (valid 10 minutes).
Step 2 with the email code: signed in with `mfa=false` (no approvals until TOTP is used).
A new access token. The refresh token rotates; a reused old one ends all the user's sessions.

End this session: the refresh token (cookie) and the session the access token names are revoked
and the cookie cleared.

get.description: The signed-in staff member (name, role, languages, alert channels) for the screen header.

post.description:
A new authenticator seed for the signed-in user (active only after /totp/confirm). Replacing an
active authenticator needs a TOTP sign-in (D4) and the user is told by email.
The first code from the app switches TOTP on. Sign in again to get an MFA session.
Change the password (ends every other session).

Recovery: a code to the work address. Always 202 (nobody learns which addresses exist); 429 when
the rate limit for this IP or this typed address is reached (the same for unknown addresses, M3).
L6: the code is mailed after the response, so a real address answers as fast as an unknown one.
Recovery step 2: the emailed code + a new password (min 12 characters); every session ends.

post.description:

Move the deal to another stage (rules in §5; LOST needs a reason). `expected_version` guards
against overwriting a newer change (409).
§11.3 Edit then approve: a new version; below the minimum goes to the manager first (D3).
Manager/MD takes over (AI off) or hands the conversation back (AI on).

§12 below-minimum alert, manager (MFA): set an approved special price (may be below the range, D3);
it becomes a price the AI may state, and `resume_ai` hands the chat back to the AI.

§7A.1 / D24: the manager (or MD) reopens a LOST deal to the stage it was lost from; the AI stays
paused until a person resumes it.
§14 practical notes: record that the salesperson shared a personal contact with the buyer.

§14 / D21: reply to the buyer on the same channel and company number, signed with the
salesperson's name. Goes through the outbound gate (consent, opt-out, 24-hour rule); a price that is
not in an approved quote is refused (422 `unapproved_price`). WhatsApp after 24 h of buyer silence
answers 422 `window_closed`: send again with `reopen_template=true`. The AI stops replying.

§14: click-to-call through the company number. The salesperson's phone rings first, then the
buyer; logged on the deal. Refused (422 `opt_out`) when the buyer asked not to be called.

§8.1 step 4: the salesperson records a stop (and the buyer's own reason, if given) after a
conversation the buyer started. Same effect as a STOP: suppression list, queued follow-ups cancelled,
Opted out badge, LOST proposed. Add only; a stop is never removed here.

§15.1 / D20: the salesperson (human, MFA) confirms the advance; every detail is optional. The deal
moves to PAYMENT.
§15.2: WON (mandatory) with an optional expected re-order date; the order record is created.

patch.description:

configured). §3 / §5 step 14: the deal's salesperson (or the colleague covering them) updates it, as
do the manager and the MD; cancelling an order is not in the SRS's salesperson list, so it stays with
the manager / MD.
